name: simdjson experimental_json_builder (C++26 reflection-based JSON serializer)
workload: Serializing native C++ structs to JSON using C++26 static reflection (P2996), measured on the twitter.json corpus and on an artificial/synthetic JSON dataset, reported in MB/s
claimed_speedup: 19x faster than nlohmann/json on Twitter data (M3 Max), 36x faster on artificial data (M3 Max); 16x faster on Twitter data (Intel Ice Lake), 28x faster on artificial data (Intel Ice Lake); 'roughly twice as fast as reflect-cpp'; hand-written code still 10-20% faster than the reflection-generated code
compiler_and_flags: clang++ from the Bloomberg experimental clang-p2996 fork (implements P2996 reflection); project sets -freflection -stdlib=libc++ -std=c++26, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (confirmed in repo's CMakeLists.txt)
hardware: Apple M3 Max MacBook Pro; an Intel Ice Lake machine (exact SKU not given)
tradeoffs: Requires an experimental, non-shipping C++26 compiler (Bloomberg's clang-p2996 fork with -freflection) rather than any release toolchain, so the technique is not usable in production yet. Same post reports it as ~2x faster than reflect-cpp (getml/reflect-cpp, an existing reflection-based serialization library) though exact reflect-cpp throughput numbers are not tabulated on the page. Hand-written (non-reflective) serialization code remains 10-20% faster than the generated code.
caveats: The repo's own README states 'THIS REPOSITORY IS OBSOLETE. The functionality is part of the simdjson library' (github.com/simdjson/simdjson, which is already catalogued) - i.e. this prototype's work is being folded into simdjson proper, so its long-term canonical home may end up being the already-known simdjson/simdjson repo rather than this standalone one. The benchmark also required a hand-built experimental compiler (via Docker or a from-source Clang build), so the numbers cannot be reproduced with any released compiler today. Ice Lake CPU model is named only by microarchitecture family, not exact SKU.
found_via: Blog: Daniel Lemire, "Reflection-based JSON in C++ at Gigabytes per Second" (lemire.me, 2024-08-13), found via query "CppCon talk static reflection serialization code generation performance"; corroborated by the identically-titled CppCon 2025 talk (simdjson.github.io/simdjson_talks/cppcon2025) and the project's own README/CMakeLists on GitHub.
